items.prompt_text:
A franchise group shares cash between four divisions each month.
- Flagship: starts with $300, earns $0/month in other revenue, spends $600/month. It sells 50 units/month at a set price.
- Supply: starts with $100, earns $30/month in other revenue, spends $50/month.
- Brand: starts with $50, earns $20/month in other revenue, spends $60/month.
- Outlet: starts with $150, earns $130/month in other revenue, spends $80/month.
- Each month Outlet sends $35 to Flagship, but only as much as it can afford that month.
- Each month Flagship sends $75 to Supply, but only as much as it can afford that month.
- Each month Supply sends $50 to Brand, but only as much as it can afford that month.

Resolve each month in this order: every division first books its other revenue and any sales income and pays its costs; then the transfers happen in the order listed above. A balance is checked at the end of the month.

Flagship sells 50 units/month; its price is yours to set. What is the lowest whole-dollar price at which NO division ends any of the 24 months with a negative balance? Reply with only that number and no other figures.

How many dollars are left for the Equity tranche? Reply with only that number and no other figures.

Five banks A, B, C, D and E are linked by interbank loans. Each holds a capital buffer that absorbs losses: A=$50, B=$80, C=$60, D=$300, E=$45. The loans (debtor → creditor: amount) are: A owes B $100; B owes C $120; C owes E $70; D owes E $55; B owes D $40. An external shock hits bank A with a $120 loss. Resolve the cascade until no further bank defaults; if two banks would default at the same time, the one earlier in the order A, B, C, D, E is taken first.

List every bank that defaults, in the order they fail, from first to last. Give the bank letters in order.

When Bank A defaults, it pays the full face value of its outgoing loan to Bank B, which is $100. However, this payment does not affect the default condition for Bank B based on its original buffer and incoming losses.

Banks B, C, and E also have their interbank incoming losses exceeding their buffers:
- Bank B has incoming losses of $100 > buffer of $80.
- Bank C has incoming losses of $120 > buffer of $60.
- Bank E has incoming losses of $125 > buffer of $45.

Bank D has incoming losses of $40 <= buffer of $300, so it does not default.

Similarly, Bank C defaults next, and Bank E defaults last among C and E, with C being earlier than E.

Thus, the order of defaults is A first, then B, then C, then E. Bank D does not default.

**Order of failure:** A, B, C, E

**Banks that default:** A, B, C, E

Five banks A, B, C, D and E are linked by interbank loans. Each holds a capital buffer that absorbs losses: A=$50, B=$80, C=$60, D=$300, E=$45. A bank defaults when its total incoming losses exceed its buffer; on default it passes the full face value of every loan it owes to its creditor (loss given default = 100%). The loans (debtor → creditor: amount) are: A owes B $100; B owes C $120; C owes E $70; D owes E $55; B owes D $40. An external shock hits bank A with a $120 loss. Resolve the cascade until no further bank defaults; if two banks would default at the same time, the one earlier in the order A, B, C, D, E is taken first.

A one-time buffer top-up to which single bank prevents the most failures overall? Reply with just that bank's letter.

Net operating income (NOI) is $130 in month 1 and grows 2% each month thereafter, so NOI in month t = 130 × 1.02^(t−1). Scheduled debt service steps up over time: $80/month in months 1–3, $110/month in months 4–6, and $140/month in months 7–12. Consider the 12-month horizon.

What is the DSCR in month 1? Give your answer as a decimal.

DSCR = 130 / 80 = 1.625

This value is above 1.25, so the covenant is not breached in month 1.

A property loan carries a covenant requiring its Debt Service Coverage Ratio (DSCR = net operating income ÷ debt service) to stay at or above 1.25 every month; the covenant is breached only when the DSCR falls strictly below 1.25 (a DSCR of exactly 1.25 passes). Net operating income (NOI) is $130 in month 1 and grows 2% each month thereafter, so NOI in month t = 130 × 1.02^(t−1). Scheduled debt service steps up over time: $80/month in months 1–3, $110/month in months 4–6, and $140/month in months 7–12. Consider the 12-month horizon.

Holding everything else fixed, what is the minimum constant monthly NOI growth rate that would avoid any covenant breach across all 12 months? Give your answer as a decimal to 4 places.

items.prompt_text:
You must choose between two mutually exclusive three-year projects. All cash flows occur at year-end. Project A: invest $1,000 now (year 0), then receive $600 in year 1, $500 in year 2, and $200 in year 3. Project B: invest $1,000 now, then receive $200 in year 1, $400 in year 2, and $800 in year 3. Unless a part states otherwise, discount at 8% per year.

What is the net present value of Project A at the 8% discount rate? Give your answer in dollars to the nearest cent.
items.output:
The net present value (NPV) of Project A at an 8% discount rate is calculated as follows:

- Initial investment: -$1,000 at year 0.
- Cash inflows: $600 at year 1, $500 at year 2, and $200 at year 3.

The NPV formula is:

\[ \text{NPV} = \sum \text{PV of all cash flows} \]

Where the present value (PV) of a cash flow is calculated as:

\[ \text{PV} = \frac{\text{CF}}{(1 + r)^n} \]

Here, \( r = 0.08 \) (8% discount rate) and \( n \) is the year.

The PV of the cash inflows is computed as:

- Year 1: \( \frac{600}{1.08^1} \approx 555.56 \)
- Year 2: \( \frac{500}{1.08^2} \approx 428.67 \)
- Year 3: \( \frac{200}{1.08^3} \approx 158.77 \)

Sum of PVs: \( 555.56 + 428.67 + 158.77 = 1142.99 \)

Subtract the initial investment: \( 1142.99 - 1000 = 142.99 \)

The NPV is $142.99 when rounded to the nearest cent.

You must choose between two mutually exclusive three-year projects. All cash flows occur at year-end. Project A: invest $1,000 now (year 0), then receive $600 in year 1, $500 in year 2, and $200 in year 3. Project B: invest $1,000 now, then receive $200 in year 1, $400 in year 2, and $800 in year 3. Unless a part states otherwise, discount at 8% per year.

At what single discount rate do the two projects have equal NPV (the crossover rate)? Give your answer as a decimal to 4 places.

\]

Rounded to four decimal places, \( r = 0.1061 \).

This rate makes the NPVs of both projects equal, as it satisfies the condition for the crossover point.
